_comment: Cross-session KV pool broker config. Read AT CALL TIME (parse cached on mtime_ns+size), so editing this file retunes every live agent session within ~5s WITH NO RELAUNCH. Resolution order per key: environment variable > this file > the module default. Remove the 'backend' key to disable the broker entirely — every caller then falls back to its configured defaults, which is the pre-broker behaviour. See ops/pool-broker.md.
_throttle_comment: Child-concurrency throttle. The GATE is prefill capacity (scheduler slots + backlog drain time + pool residency); runtime free VRAM is only a FLOOR backstop — see clients/hermes/docs/prefill-capacity-throttle.md for why, and client rule 15 for the general trap. Every default below is derived from a measurement on ONE deployment: re-measure before trusting a magnitude. Omit a key to use its default.

total_stream_cap.what: TOTAL concurrent streams the backend may carry, MAINS INCLUDED. The single knob for 'push things harder'.
total_stream_cap.derivation: There is NO interior aggregate maximum below --max-running-requests: aggregate decode rises monotonically with concurrency on both pool geometries measured. So the cap cannot be read off the aggregate curve and must be keyed on a LANE's own share of its solo rate — the number a human is actually reading. 2 is the largest concurrency at which a lane keeps about two thirds of itself. Authoritative curve: BENCHMARKS.md §3.20 (queue-filtered). Raising it buys aggregate throughput at a lane's expense, which is a product decision, which is why it is a runtime key and not a constant.

stream_cap.what: Cross-session stream target for a larger server. The live max_running_requests and total_stream_cap both still bound it; requests beyond the server's slots queue.

cache_reserve_frac.what: Fraction of the pool kept as prefix-cache slack and never handed out. usable = pool - cache_reserve, and every granted ceiling is water-filled out of usable.

main_slot_reserve.what: Scheduler slots held for EACH live main before any child is admitted. A main that cannot get a slot waits however much pool and VRAM are free, and every main needs a slot for its own control-plane calls (compaction, titling, the goal judge). 2 also protects one auxiliary call per main.

prefill_rate_tps.what: Fallback prefill throughput, used only until the live counters have accumulated.
prefill_rate_tps.derivation: Prefer SELF-CALIBRATION from the server's own cumulative counters: total_prefill_uncached_tokens / total_prefill_busy_us. That divisor then survives a model swap, a quantisation change or a card change with nobody editing a constant. The default here is one measurement of that ratio (8,481 tok/s; independently 8,377 an hour later on the same lane; log-derived chunk-saturated median 8,958, p25-p75 7,257-10,191).

drain_budget_s.what: How long the uncached waiting backlog may take to drain before children are refused.
drain_budget_s.derivation: NOT a round number: it is the control-plane goal-judge timeout, past which the judge times out and an autonomous loop can halt. Tie a drain budget to the deadline it protects.

waste_base_tokens.what: Measured wasted prefill per call with NO contention — tokens the server recomputed beyond genuine prompt growth, i.e. the cached prefix was evicted.

waste_growth.what: Multiplier on that waste per added concurrent stream, fitted through the measured 114,385 wasted tokens at five other in-flight requests. ⛔ This curve depends entirely on YOUR prefix sizes — see client rule 12.

prefill_alloc_mib.what: Largest single allocation MEASURED to be fatal (a prefill CUDA OOM whose own message read 'Tried to allocate 560.00 MiB ... 280.94 MiB is free').

prefill_transient_mib.what: Per-in-flight-prefill transient VRAM after the bounded-gather fix: flat at every context length, down from 1,024 MiB at 512K. The VRAM FLOOR is prefill_alloc_mib + max_running_requests * prefill_transient_mib = 688 MiB at mrr 4. Below it, admit nothing and let in-flight work drain; above it, VRAM contributes no cap at all.

vram_hold_max_s.what: How long a child dispatch is held while the floor leg is critical, before it proceeds anyway. Bounded on purpose: an OOM that kills the lane for every session is worse than a slow dispatch, but a permanently stalled agent is worse than a risked one.

hot_token_usage.what: POOL-MEMORY pressure rung for window sizing. Memory pressure is what a memory rule is for; queueing is a prefill-throughput effect and belongs to the prefill gate.

_not_tunable_at_runtime.REFRESH_S: 5.0 — how old the allowance may be before a reader refreshes it
_not_tunable_at_runtime.STALE_S: 30.0 — past this the allowance returns None and callers use their configured defaults
_not_tunable_at_runtime.VRAM_SAMPLE_MAX_AGE_S: 90.0 — four consecutive misses: the publisher is GONE, not busy. Past it the sample is discarded, not trusted
_not_tunable_at_runtime.MAIN_WINDOW_FLOOR: 64000 — the actual floor a main window is clamped to
_not_tunable_at_runtime.GUARANTEED_LANE_WINDOW: 131072 — the share a lane is guaranteed BEFORE lending. ⛔ NOT a floor; at five live mains the grant drops to 65,536
_not_tunable_at_runtime.WINDOW_GRID: 8192 — windows are chosen on this grid: legible, and aligned to the engine's paging
_not_tunable_at_runtime.ALLOCATE_BUDGET_MS: 200 — a pluggable policy that exceeds this is dropped for that refresh
